tests.question:
For calendar tax year 2025, Company A is a domestic C corporation that acts as the purchasing corporation in a qualified stock purchase (QSP). Company A is the common parent of a consolidated group that includes Target Corporation as the new target, and Company A will attach Target Corporation’s supplemental Form 8883 to the group’s 2025 consolidated Form 1120. Company A and the selling consolidated group's common parent timely filed a joint Internal Revenue Service Form 8023 to make an irrevocable election under Internal Revenue Code (I.R.C.) § 338(h)(10) regarding the acquisition of Target Corporation on June 1, 2023. All dollar values are stated in thousands. During the current 2025 tax year, the following subsequent events occurred:

+ A milestone event specified in the initial acquisition agreement was achieved, triggering a mandatory contingent earn-out payment of $5,300.00 thousand from Company A to the sellers on September 1, 2025.
+ Company A's tax committee determined that under the contingent-payment interest rules of § 1274, this $5,300.00 thousand outlay must be bifurcated into a $5,000.00 thousand principal adjustment and $300.00 thousand of imputed interest.
+ The historic Class I through Class VI asset allocation limits from the initial 2023 IRS Form 8883 filing were already fully exhausted at their maximum fair market values on the acquisition date.
 
Draft a comprehensive, structured technical text block for Company A's 2025 tax compliance files that explicitly details the form-filling and reporting requirements for this cross-period adjustment. In the text block, answer the following: In exactly which Part of IRS Form 8883 must the $5,000.00 thousand principal adjustment be reported under the residual method, and on precisely which tax reporting form, schedule, and line must the isolated $300.00 thousand imputed interest portion be reported?

checks.criteria: Concludes that Company A reports the $5,000.00 thousand principal adjustment on Internal Revenue Service Form 8883, Part VI, Supplemental Statement of Assets Transferred.
Concludes that Company A allocates the full $5,000.00 thousand principal adjustment to Class VII goodwill and going concern value.
Concludes that Company A reports the $300.00 thousand imputed interest on the 2025 Internal Revenue Service Form 1120, page 1, line 18, Interest.
States that no separate Form 1120 schedule applies to the $300.00 thousand amount reported on Form 1120, page 1, line 18.
Determines that Company A files a supplemental Form 8883 for calendar tax year 2025.
States that Company A completes Form 8883 Parts I through IV and Part VI for the 2025 supplemental filing.
States that form 8883 Part VI reports Company A’s redetermined Adjusted Grossed-Up Basis (AGUB) allocation.
Identifies that form 8883 Part VI identifies the previously reported asset allocation.
Identifies that form 8883 Part VI identifies the $5,000.00 thousand increase.
Identifies that form 8883 Part VI identifies the milestone earn-out payment as the reason for the increase.
Calculates that the $5,300.00 thousand contingent payment is bifurcated into $5,000.00 thousand of principal and $300.00 thousand of imputed interest under Internal Revenue Code (I.R.C.) § 1274.
States that the $300.00 thousand imputed interest is excluded from Adjusted Grossed-Up Basis (AGUB).
States that the $300.00 thousand imputed interest is excluded from Form 8883 Part VI.
States that the $300.00 thousand imputed interest is excluded from Class VII tax basis.
States that Treasury Regulation § 1.338-7 requires Company A’s redetermined Adjusted Grossed-Up Basis (AGUB) to be allocated under Treasury Regulation § 1.338-6.
Explains that Treasury Regulation § 1.338-6 applies the residual allocation method sequentially from Class I through Class VII assets.
States that allocations to Class I through Class VI assets cannot exceed their fair market values.

Determines that the increase allocated to each of Class I, Class II, Class III, Class IV, Class V, and Class VI is $0.00 thousand because their acquisition-date fair market value limits were exhausted.
Notes that the $300.00 thousand interest expense is subject to otherwise applicable deduction limitations.
Concludes that no new Internal Revenue Service Form 8023 filing is required for the 2025 earn-out adjustment.
States that Company A retains a supporting statement with the supplemental Form 8883 workpapers that explains the contingent-payment adjustment.

tests.question:
During the 2025 tax year, Solar Co began construction on a 3-megawatt (MW) solar facility on March 1, 2025, and satisfied the physical work test for beginning construction. On June 1, 2025, Solar Co suspended construction for eight months after its financing became unavailable. Construction resumed in February 2026. Solar Co intends to rely on the continuity safe harbor described in IRS Notice 2022-61 and plans to place the facility in service during 2029.
How does the eight-month construction suspension affect Solar Co's eligibility for the Internal Revenue Code § 48E Clean Electricity Investment Credit? Specifically, does the interruption prevent Solar Co from relying on the continuity safe harbor, and what is the applicable placed-in-service deadline for maintaining eligibility under Notice 2022-61?

checks.criteria: Identifies that Solar Co satisfied the physical work test by beginning physical work of a significant nature on March 1, 2025.
Concludes that Solar Co began construction before the September 2, 2025 effective date of Notice 2025-42.
Concludes that Solar Co began construction before the July 4, 2026 statutory cutoff enacted by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Explains that because construction began on March 1, 2025, the later restrictions applicable to projects beginning construction after those dates do not prevent Solar Co from qualifying for the Sec. 48E credit.
Explains that satisfying the physical work test alone does not establish Internal Revenue Code § 48E eligibility.
Explains that Solar Co must also satisfy the continuity requirement, either through the continuity safe harbor or a facts-and-circumstances analysis.
States that Notice 2022-61 provides a four-calendar-year continuity safe harbor measured from the year construction began.
Identifies December 31, 2029 as the applicable continuity safe-harbor placed-in-service deadline.
Concludes that Solar Co’s planned 2029 placed-in-service date falls within the four-year continuity safe harbor period.
Concludes that the eight-month construction pause does not automatically cause Solar Co to lose eligibility for the Sec. 48E credit or prevent reliance on the continuity safe harbor.
Explains that a temporary interruption in construction may be permissible under beginning-of-construction guidance and does not necessarily restart the beginning-of-construction date.
Concludes that if the facility is placed in service by December 31, 2029, Solar Co generally may rely on the continuity safe harbor notwithstanding the eight-month pause.
Explains that if the continuity safe harbor were not satisfied, continuity would be evaluated under a facts-and-circumstances analysis.
Identifies that documentation regarding the financing-related construction interruption would strengthen Solar Co’s position if continuity were challenged.
Correctly cites Notice 2022-61 as the governing authority for the physical work test and continuity safe harbor.
Correctly cites Notice 2013-29 as the foundational beginning-of-construction guidance incorporated into later notices.
Correctly references Notice 2025-42 when discussing post-September 2, 2025 beginning-of-construction restrictions for wind and solar projects.
Correctly references Sec. 48E(e)(4), as added by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, when discussing the accelerated termination rules for certain later-starting wind and solar projects.
Concludes that Solar Co does not restart the beginning-of-construction analysis when construction resumes in February 2026 and retains March 1, 2025 as its beginning-of-construction date.
Concludes that Notice 2025-42’s post-September 2, 2025 beginning-of-construction restrictions do not apply because Solar Co began construction on March 1, 2025.
Concludes that the July 4, 2026 beginning-of-construction cutoff under Sec. 48E(e)(4) does not apply because Solar Co began construction on March 1, 2025.

tests.question:
A domestic corporation timely filed its 2025 Form 1120 by April 15, 2026.

During an Internal Revenue Service Large Business and International examination, the corporation’s representative left the examiner a voicemail requesting net rate netting under Internal Revenue Code § 6621(d).

Is the oral request sufficient to establish a valid net rate netting claim?

If not, what written submission must the corporation make, which form must the examiner include in the case file, which form must the corporation file, and by what point in the examination must the request be submitted?

checks.criteria: Identifies that the corporation’s oral request is insufficient to establish a valid net rate netting claim.
Identifies that the corporation must submit the net rate netting request in writing under Internal Revenue Manual § 4.10.26.3.
Identifies that the corporation must submit the net rate netting request in writing under Revenue Procedure 2000-26.
Defines Form 3198 as Special Handling Notice for Examination Case Processing.
Identifies that the examiner must complete and attach Form 3198 to the examination case file.
Defines Form 843 as Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement.
Identifies that Form 843 is not required to request net rate netting, and that the corporation may instead furnish the required information in a letter or other written statement.
Identifies that the written request and required forms must be submitted before the examination is closed.
